tweets.text:
The way we execute large trades onchain is outdated.

It's also unnecessarily expensive when liquidity is thin.

Try selling $100K worth of an altcoin through an average orderbook size. Nearly impossible.

Without enough buyers, parts of your order can fill at lower prices.

While exploring shielded trading, @silhouette_ex found that larger traders were more worried about tipping off the market before making a trade.

This is precisely the feedback that helped shape their RFQ system, which is already live for @xStocksFi and now expanding to BTC and HYPE perps on @HyperliquidX.

Here's how it works:

→ Request a price for the entire trade
→ Market makers compete with quotes
→ Accept the quote you prefer

All perp trades still execute through Hyperliquid's orderbook. Better prices in the book get priority, while the market maker fills the remainder at the agreed price.

Large trades need this kind of flexibility.
Gud tek.
